1. HEADQUARTERS AND ORGANISATIONAL DETAILS

The Shelter Operations Coordination Unit (SOCU, referred to internally as “the Unit”) is the state-level coordination body responsible for the planning, activation, and demobilisation of emergency shelter operations across Victoria. The Unit operates under the direction of the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) Emergency Management Branch and liaises with local councils, the Australian Red Cross, and the Victorian State Emergency Service (VICSES).

SOCU administrative records state that the Shelter Operations Coordination Unit headquarters location is Melbourne, Victoria. Record status: current. This entry is current as of the date of this log and has been verified against the Unit’s establishment charter (ref. SOCU-CH-001). All operational planning, rostering, and fleet management functions are administered from this location. No change of headquarters has been proposed or scheduled within the period covered by this log.

2. OPERATIONAL OVERVIEW – JANUARY 2023

SOCU Administrative Log – Headquarters and Operations Overview

Classification: Internal

1. HEADQUARTERS AND ORGANISATIONAL DETAILS

The Shelter Operations Coordination Unit (SOCU, referred to internally as “the Unit”) is the state-level coordination body responsible for the planning, activation, and demobilisation of emergency shelter operations across Victoria. The Unit operates under the direction of the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) Emergency Management Branch and liaises with local councils, the Australian Red Cross, and the Victorian State Emergency Service (VICSES).

SOCU administrative records state that the Shelter Operations Coordination Unit headquarters location is Melbourne, Victoria. Record status: current. This entry is current as of the date of this log and has been verified against the Unit’s establishment charter (ref. SOCU-CH-001). All operational planning, rostering, and fleet management functions are administered from this location. No change of headquarters has been proposed or scheduled within the period covered by this log.

2. OPERATIONAL OVERVIEW – JANUARY 2023

01/01/2023 – New Year’s Day public holiday. Unit skeleton staff only. No shelter activations reported. Ops room stood down at 1700 hrs. (JB)

02/01/2023 – Resumption of normal duties. Morning briefing held at 0830 hrs in the Melbourne HQ conference room. Agenda items: review of summer heatwave response plan, update on staff training compliance, and allocation of fleet for upcoming community education sessions. Minutes recorded by LM. (JB)

05/01/2023 – Receipt of new emergency shelter signage order (12 x A-frame boards, 8 x roller banners). Delivered to HQ storage bay B. Inventory logged by SW. Signage to be distributed to regional offices ahead of the summer season. (SW)

09/01/2023 – Staff meeting (weekly) at 0900 hrs. Attendance: 14 staff members. Discussion on the upcoming heatwave season – Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) forecast indicates above-average temperatures for February. Consideration given to pre-positioning of shelter kits in northern Victoria. Action item: TL to draft a pre-positioning proposal for the 15/01 meeting. (JB)

12/01/2023 – Vehicle maintenance – Vehicle #4 (Toyota HiAce) serviced at authorised fleet provider. Oil change, brake inspection, and new tyres fitted. Cost: $1,240.00. Receipt attached to expense claim SOCU-EXP-0123-04. Vehicle returned to HQ pool 1400 hrs. (SW)

15/01/2023 – Weekly planning meeting (special session) at 1000 hrs. Pre-positioning proposal reviewed and approved in principle. Four (4) shelter kits to be staged at the Bendigo and Wodonga depots. Kits to include 20 x swags, 20 x sleeping bags, 20 x emergency blankets, and 20 x hygiene packs. Logistics to confirm transport schedule with depot managers by 20/01. (TL)

18/01/2023 – Office supplies order placed: printer toner (x12), A4 paper (x20 reams), pens (x50), and notepads (x30). Order reference SOCU-OFF-0118. Expected delivery 25/01. (LM)

22/01/2023 – Community education session conducted at the Melbourne Town Hall (10:00–14:00). SOCU staff provided information on personal emergency preparedness and shelter options. Approx. 60 members of the public attended. Feedback forms collected; summary to be collated by KM. (KM)

25/01/2023 – Office supplies order received and checked against delivery docket. All items present. Toner cartridges stored in the stationery cupboard (Room 2.14). Paper and notepads distributed to staff. (LM)

documents.title: SEOC Situation Report - Harbourview Community Centre Status
documents.content:
The incident affecting the Wattle Creek Caravan Park and surrounding low-lying areas of the Harbourview district remains in the recovery phase. Flood waters have receded to below minor flood level at the Harbourview gauge (reading 1.2 m at 0600 hrs today, steady). The Bureau of Meteorology has cancelled the flood watch for the catchment. River debris and silt deposits continue to affect several roads, including Blackwood Rd, where a single-lane closure remains in place between the caravan park entrance and the intersection with Riverbend Drive. Council crews are scheduled to begin debris removal today.

Weather conditions are favourable for the next 48 hours. A dry, mild air mass is expected to persist, with light winds and daytime maximum temperatures around 23°C. No significant rainfall is forecast for the catchment until at least the weekend.

**2. DECLARATION STATUS**

|---|---|---|---|

No new declarations have been made since the last report. The active declaration for ED-2024-017 remains in force and will be reviewed at the end of the week.

**3. HARBOURVIEW COMMUNITY CENTRE – OPERATIONS SUMMARY**

The centre continues to operate as a combined temporary accommodation and drop-in support hub. Occupancy at 0600 hrs was 47 persons, comprising 39 residents of the Wattle Creek Caravan Park and 8 persons from nearby properties who were displaced by the flood. This is down from a peak of 68 on the night of 09/11/2024.

SEOC approval records Incident Action Plan 2024 approval date as 2024-01-10. Record status: current. The IAP 2024 remains the governing operational document for the current response and recovery activities at the centre. All site operations are being conducted in accordance with the relevant sections of the plan.

The centre is staffed by a joint team from the Department of Communities, the Australian Red Cross, and SEOC liaison officers. It is providing temporary accommodation for residents of the Wattle Creek Caravan Park who were unable to return, as well as a drop-in centre for affected residents seeking information, meals, and connection to support services. The centre will remain in an active status until the recovery phase concludes or a formal decision is made to stand it down.

**6. INCIDENT SUMMARY – WATTLE CREEK FLOOD (continued)**

Floodwaters in the Wattle Creek catchment continue to recede. The gauge at Wattle Creek Bridge recorded 2.1 m at 0600 hrs on 15/11/2024, down from a peak of 3.4 m on 10/11/2024. Minor road closures remain in place on Gundagai Road and Old Binya Road due to debris and soft edges. The SES advises that these roads are expected to reopen by 17/11/2024, subject to inspection.

Sandbag removal has commenced at properties on River Street and Wattle Street. Residents returning to their properties are reminded to wear appropriate protective clothing and to check with the Recovery Centre before re-entering homes that sustained water ingress. A hazardous waste collection point has been established at the southern end of the Wattle Creek Caravan Park, operating 0900–1500 hrs daily.

A second, smaller release of water from the Binya Weir occurred at 0230 hrs on 15/11/2024. This release was within operational parameters and did not result in additional inundation. Downstream properties on the Binya Flats were notified via the standard alert system.

**7. HARBOURVIEW COMMUNITY CENTRE – OPERATIONAL UPDATE**

The centre continues to operate as a temporary accommodation and drop-in support hub. Occupancy at 0600 hrs on 15/11/2024 was 41 persons, comprising 35 residents of the Wattle Creek Caravan Park, 5 persons from nearby properties, and 1 person transferred from the Binya Neighbourhood House following its closure. This is down from a peak of 68 on the night of 09/11/2024.

Meals are being provided three times daily. The last meal service of the evening is at 1830 hrs. Laundry facilities are available between 0800 and 2000 hrs. A dedicated quiet room has been set aside for families with young children.

The centre is staffed by a joint team from the Department of Communities, the Australian Red Cross, and SEOC liaison officers. It is providing temporary accommodation for residents of the Wattle Creek Caravan Park who were unable to return, as well as a drop-in centre for affected residents seeking information, meals, and connection to support services.
